title: Understanding — Seal — payload
description: The first party (the joining party) proposes a bilateral agreement, through a handshake modelled on (but not conforming to) IEEE 7012-2025, grounded in a passed understanding/exchange; the second party (the host) accepts it, refuses it, or counters with a single alternative. All three are decisions, reported in the response (SPEC §8, "A decision is not a failure") — see spec.md Authorization. The outer document members (id, type, issuer, recipient, issuedAt, expiresAt, proof) are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.

exchangeId.description: The `id` of the understanding/exchange response this seal is grounded in. Its recorded outcome MUST be "understood". Grounds at most one seal negotiation — see spec.md Authorization, "One negotiation per exchange".

respondsTo.description: Present only on the single follow-up permitted after a counter: the `id` of the understanding/seal request the second party countered. See spec.md Authorization, "Answering a counter", for the conditions a recipient MUST check before accepting this follow-up rather than refusing it with understanding/seal:negotiationExhausted.

Response.title: Understanding — Seal — response payload
Response.description: The second party's decision on the request named by taskContext — accepted, countered or refused — bound by taskDigestMultibase per SPEC §4.9.3 and §7.3 item 20.5's first binding form, so this response can serve as this specification's declared outcome evidence (see spec.md front matter, outcomeEvidence). A signed refusal or counter is evidence of the same kind as a signed acceptance; a party citing this response as the record that an agreement was reached MUST check that `decision` is `accepted`.

decision.description: The second party's decision, per spec.md Authorization: `accepted` seals the proposed agreement; `countered` offers the single alternative carried in `counterAgreement` (never in answer to a request that carries `respondsTo`); `refused` declines outright, with no reason given or owed.

taskContext.description: The `id` of the understanding/seal request this response decides — the initiating document of this exchange per SPEC §4.9.1. For an acceptance, this is the original proposal unless a counter was answered, in which case it is the follow-up request that re-proposed the countered terms.

taskDigestMultibase.description: The task digest of the request named by `taskContext`, computed per SPEC §4.9.3 as multibase(multihash(H(JCS(document ∖ proof)))) over the FULL request document — not merely its `agreement` member — so the binding also covers `exchangeId` and, where present, `respondsTo`.

counterAgreement.description: The second party's single alternative agreement, drawn from the same roster, per IEEE 7012-2025 §5.3.1(b). Present exactly when `decision` is `countered`: the schema refuses it beside any other decision, and spec.md Response requires it with `countered`.
